subject: social_science

concepts.title: Prejudice Definition
concepts.definition: Holding a negative opinion or judgment about individuals or groups without knowing the facts, often based on their identity.
concepts.key_idea: Judging others negatively before knowing them.
question_patterns: what does it mean to be prejudiced
how do prejudices form about others
explain the meaning of judging others negatively

solution_steps.action: calculate the impact of negative bias
solution_steps.explain: prejudice is the difference between an irrational negative judgment and actual evidence

concepts.title: Stereotype Formation
concepts.definition: The act of fitting diverse individuals into a single, rigid image or pattern based on their group identity.
concepts.key_idea: Generalizing traits to an entire group.
question_patterns: give an example of a common stereotype
how does society create fixed images

solution_steps.action: calculate the scope of a stereotype
solution_steps.explain: a stereotype multiplies a single trait across a whole group

concepts.title: Discrimination Mechanism
concepts.definition: The unfair treatment of people based on their background, often resulting from acting upon prejudices or stereotypes.
concepts.key_idea: Acting on negative beliefs to deny rights.
question_patterns: how does discrimination differ from prejudice
list ways people are discriminated against
why is discrimination harmful to equality

solution_steps.action: calculate the intensity of discriminatory acts
solution_steps.explain: discrimination is the product of acting on bias and excluding others

worked_examples.question_pattern: If a person judges a group negatively without evidence, the {prejudice_score} is high.

solution_template.explain: prejudice exists when evidence is absent

worked_examples.question_pattern: When a single trait is applied to {group_size} people, a stereotype is formed.

solution_template.explain: the stereotype covers the entire group
